key_insight: Embedding optoelectronic mechanosensors into suction cups enables local, distributed sensing that lets a soft octopus‑inspired arm infer contact forces and object positions at the periphery, supporting autonomous underwater grasping with minimal central computation.
problem_solved: How to achieve robust, responsive underwater grasping with soft robots despite limited central sensing, noisy dynamics, and communication delays by moving perception and control closer to the sensors.
method: Design of a soft robotic arm with suction‑cup end‑effectors instrumented with low‑power optoelectronic mechanosensors to measure local contact forces.
Distributed peripheral processing that interprets sensor signals to estimate object position/contact state at each suction cup.
Closed‑loop grasp control that leverages local force/position estimates for autonomous, coordinated grasping without heavy central computation.
impact: Demonstrates an embodied, edge‑centric sensing/control paradigm useful for AI/ML practitioners building real‑world robotic systems—reducing latency, bandwidth, and learning complexity for manipulation in challenging environments.
visual_elements: Annotated schematic of the soft arm showing sensorized suction cups and signal flow from sensors to peripheral processors

paper_title: Peripheral control enabled by distributed sensing in an octopus-inspired soft robotic arm for autonomous underwater grasping
paper_authors: Emanuela Del Dottore, Romina Adhami, Ebrahim Shahabi, Emanuele Solfiti, Michele Martini
